title: Venue: leaders and groups
description: Venue track. Whom to host, your own payment and cancellation terms, supporting a group before arrival, on site and after.

objectives.text: Assess a leader before the contract by their own audience, program, contract with a co-leader and past groups
Build your own payment schedule, minimum and cancellation scale from your obligations, and test them against a short group
Split the steps of supporting a group before arrival, on site and after, with one point of contact

checks.question: A leader promises a full group thanks to a co-leader's large audience. What does the course suggest a venue rely on?
options: The co-leader's audience: it is bigger
The leader's own circle and past groups; the partner's audience is a bonus
Nothing: the minimum will protect anyway
checks.explain: A group is gathered by the leader's own circle. A minimum is not built on a partner's audience (u1, "What can be checked before the contract").

checks.question: A venue has received leaders' prepayments for retreats six months away. How does the course suggest treating them?
options: Spend them on running costs: the money has been received
Treat them as an obligation, do not spend them on running costs, and keep them so they can be returned
Invest them in renovation before the season
Return them to the leaders straight away
checks.explain: A prepayment is an obligation until the service is provided. A venue spending it on running costs funds itself with someone else's money (u2, "Where the money is kept").

checks.question: Why does the leader have one point of contact at the venue?
options: So answers do not diverge: one person is responsible for the group before, during and after
So the leader does not talk to the kitchen
checks.explain: When questions go to different people, the answers diverge. One point of contact holds the whole group (u3).
